News.title: Brigitte is wary of women ‘predators’ looking to work with Macron bombshell book claims after ‘texts to actress’
News.content:
'VERY JEALOUS' Brigitte is wary of women ‘predators’ looking to work with Macron bombshell book claims after ‘texts to actress’

BRIGITTE Macron is convinced all women are predators out to steal her husband, the reporter behind the “flirty texts” bombshell claims.

The French power couple have been ensnared in scandal over reports that Emmanuel Macron had a “platonic love affair” with an Iranian actress.





The jealous first lady of France was also caught on camera shoving her husband in the face moments before disembarking from a flight to Vietnam.

The president insisted they were just “squabbling and joking” but insiders gossip that Brigitte’s much younger husband has been romping with lovers, both male and female, throughout his time in office.

The politician was just 15 when he started a relationship with the then mother-of-three, his French literature teacher.

Now, a ruthless expose claims that Brigitte Macron “has always known that women are predators… and that’s why she’s wary of them”.

“This has undoubtedly contributed to the fact that the president is mostly surrounded by men”, the author Florian Tardif added.

Tardif is the political editor of Paris Match magazine and his new book, A (Nearly) Perfect Couple, has skewered the French power couple.

But a scan of Macron’s ministers since he came into power nine years ago confirms the author’s hunch.

Only one of the president’s seven appointees was a women – and grey-haired Élisabeth Borne did not even last two years.



Tardif described Borne as: “a Diet Coke addict and compulsive vaper who understood from the outset that she was only there to tick a box”.

He also claimed that Brigitte sneaked glances at photos of women applying for jobs on the phones of advisors before banning Macron from hiring them.

She would reportedly scream “Show me!” and then, if she felt the woman was too attractive, she would say: “She won’t be coming to the Élysée!”



Comments like this were “enough to seal her fate, even before she’s considered”, wrote political journalist Tardif.

“She’s very jealous”, he added.

A close ally of the first lady allegedly told the author that Brigitte “got rid” of female advisors.

According to Tardiff, the 73-year-old accelerated the departure of an intern in her twenties who allegedly tried to “use seduction to get where she wanted” in the Élysée Palace.

But the first lady has denied all allegations of snooping and hiring interference.



Her representatives told Le Parisien: “Brigitte Macron categorically denied this account directly to the author on March 5, specifying that she never looks at her husband’s mobile phone.”

Iranian actress Golshifteh Farahani has also consistently denied any romantic involvement with Macron in the past.

But in an interview with Bild, Tardif said: “Everything I wrote is 100 per cent certain.

“Four independent individuals from the president’s political entourage gave me the same explanation.

“There was indeed a platonic affair between the president and the actress.”



Many of her other relationships have remained private from the public.

It was also Tardif who revealed that Brigitte raged “I want her scalp” after reading flirty texts between Macron and the Iranian actress.

In one message, Farahani reportedly told Macron, “I find you very attractive.”

Macron, according to Tardif, also told Farahani “You are very beautiful.”

Brigitte, 73, is desperately afraid that Emmanuel, 48, will leave her.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The first lady told friends last year: “I’m afraid. Afraid of having done all of this, for him to abandon me”.

News.title: Almost 50 children a WEEK being arrested for dealing drugs including heroin & cocaine with some aged just 11
News.content:
DRUG-DEALING KIDS Almost 50 children a WEEK being arrested for dealing drugs including heroin & cocaine with some aged just 11

NEARLY 50 kids a week — some as young as 11 — were arrested for drug dealing last year, shock figures reveal.

They were nicked for selling narcotics including heroin, crack and cocaine.



A Sun on Sunday Freedom of Information probe revealed 2,466 under-17s were held on suspicion of dealing drugs in 2025 — 47.5 per week.

The number has soared by 1,000 since 2023 when 1,439 children were arrested.



County lines gangs are feared to have exploited nearly 12,000 kids into working for them.

Shocking cases in the past year include an 11-year-old in Suffolk suspected of dealing cannabis, a boy of 12 held over suspected Class A drug offences in Essex and a 12-year-old girl in Norfolk nicked for suspected crack-cocaine dealing.

The figures also revealed youngsters dealing in ketamine and nitrous oxide “laughing gas” and psychoactive substances.

Leicestershire had the most arrests — 277 children held on suspicion of dealing.



It is followed by Greater Manchester (171), London (162) and Essex (160).

Kids’ charity Barnardo’s said: “Children involved are groomed, coerced and threatened.”

Det Supt Dan Mitchell, of the National County Lines Coordination Centre, said: “The exploitation of children remains a significant concern.

“Children caught up in county lines are increasingly recognised as victims. We estimate as many as 11,600 are at risk.”

News.title: Ex-cop turned pimp is living in Britain on benefits while facing jail in Poland for running prostitution ring
News.content:
JAIL SWERVE Ex-cop turned pimp is living in Britain on benefits while facing jail in Poland for running prostitution ring

A POLISH former cop convicted of running an international prostitution ring has been living in Britain on benefits while avoiding prison back home.

Julius Taylor, 50, was found guilty in 2018 of violently forcing four young women into the sex trade.





He was sentenced in his absence to seven years in a Polish prison, but is fighting extradition while living in a Peterborough council flat with his mum, 72, as her carer.

He gets £600 a month in Universal Credit, according to extradition paperwork.

Taylor forced victims into prostitution in Germany and the Netherlands after promising them waitress jobs or trips to see relatives.

One victim in Poland was kidnapped.



He beat another.

Taylor, who was a community cop in Poland, came to Britain in 1997 and drove lorries in Spalding, Lincs.

It is understood his offending happened on extended visits home from 2003 to 2004.

He was arrested by UK cops in 2024 and a court agreed his extradition last month, with Judge Grace Leong telling him the “gravity” of his crimes “cannot be understated”.



But he remains here as he is appealing the decision.

News.title: Shocking moment shameless fly-tippers are caught on CCTV dumping rubbish on street as they are slapped with £2,300 fine
News.content:
THIS is the moment fly-tippers were caught dumping rubbish in a residential street while wearing flip flops.

CCTV footage from the street shows three men jumping out of a white Ford Transit van and dumping a pile of trash in Harrow, London.





One of the men identified, Marius Grancea, was fined £2,337 and warned he would be sent to jail if he did it again.

Footage from Weighton Road shows the vehicle stopping on the side of the road on April 18, 2025.

Two of the men come out of the van with hoodies covering their heads and flip flops on their feet.

The fly tippers open the back of the vehicle, stuffed with items, and quickly carry them to industrial bins next to the residential homes.

With black bags and beige mattresses in their hands, the culprits dump the rubbish onto the side of the road.

After being caught red-handed on Harrow Council’s CCTV cameras, the authority identified Marius Grancea as one of the men.

He was taken to court on April 9 and pleaded guilty to his actions.

Grancea, from Enfield in London, was ordered to pay £2,337 and was told that he faced custody if he was caught offending again.



A Harrow spokesperson said: “Three men and a white van were dumping waste on Weighton Road.

“Their quick ‘trash and dash’ was caught on our CCTV camera.

“Our officers moved fast. They found one of them and took them to court

“Marius Grancea from Enfield pleaded guilty. Judge said it was deliberate. Ordered to pay £2,337 for the crime and warned they risk custody if found to do it again

“We’re getting tough on criminal dumpers.”

News.title: Gunman shot dead by Secret Service after opening fire outside the White House as video shows reporter diving for cover
News.content:
GUNSHOTS have been fired outside the White House, forcing a lockdown – while Donald Trump was inside, negotiating the Iran peace deal.

The suspected gunman was shot after he fired at the agents near a checkpoint.





He was taken to hospital in a critical condition but later died from his injuries.

Another bystander was also injured.

The Secret Service said that according to a preliminary investigation, the person approached a checkpoint, removed a weapon from his bag and began firing at posted officers.”

The FBI, police and security forces swarmed the area, while members of the press were forced to take shelter inside.

Footage shows Secret Service officers armed with rifles patrolling on the North Lawn of the residence.

A number of journalists were in the middle of taping their news reports about the looming US-Iran deal when the first sounds of gunfire sounded.

Secret Service agents immediately shouted “get down” and warned of “shots fired.”

Senior White House Correspondent for ABC News, Selina Wang, was in the middle of taping a news report when she was forced to duck for cover.



A video she shared on X shows the sheer terror on her face amid the live fire in the near distance before she “sprinted” inside the briefing room.

“Many gunshots were heard when we were at the White House. We were told to run into the press briefing room,” she added.

NBC News Correspondent Julie Tsirkin said that an estimated 20 to 30 shots were fired.



“Secret service told those of us gathered on the north lawn to run inside the press briefing room,” she said.

“USSS officers, gun drawn, told us to run inside. White House now on lockdown.”

On X, Secret Service said it was “aware of reports of shots fired near 17th Street and Pennsylvania Avenue NW” – one block from the White House — and was “working to corroborate the information with personnel on the ground.”



In a social media post, FBI Director Kash Patel said officers are responding to shots fired and said he would “update the public as we’re able.”

The investigation is still ongoing and there is still a significant police presence near the scene.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The lockdown comes a month after the shooting at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner.

News.title: Nigel Farage’s plan to lift burden on workers is a breath of fresh air as Labour plans to raid their pockets instead
News.content:
Labour’s only idea is picking pockets

LABOUR’S leadership rivals have had a busy week planning raids on the pockets of hard-working Brits.

On Thursday Wes Streeting set out his plan for a wealth tax that would clobber workers by jacking up the capital gains levy to rake in an extra £12billion.





On Friday Andy Burnham countered with his own land tax plans, which would fleece homeowners just because the value of their property has risen.

The “King of the North” says he believes land in the UK is undertaxed. If so, it must be the only thing in this country which is.

These pretenders to the Number Ten crown can’t imagine wealth creation because they are hooked on taxation.

In this climate a policy which actually lifts the burden on workers is as rare as hen’s teeth.

So Nigel Farage’s plan to abolish tax on overtime is like a breath of fresh air.

Just think of it, a move that incentivises people to actually work longer and take home more of their hard-earned cash.

Reform claims it would make a newly qualified nurse £1,300 a year better off and put £700 more in the pocket of a warehouse worker.

Of course these plans need to be fully costed and scrutinised.



But what a difference to the rhetoric of Streeting and Burnham.

Getting the taxman off the back of workers and allowing them to spend more of their own money would actually help voters and the economy.

Yet a tax-cutting policy from anyone aiming to lead Labour is as about as likely as Jeremy Corbyn joining the Tories.

Few bob for builders

ALAN Milburn says a £718billion UK building bonanza is the perfect opportunity for construction firms to invest in young Brits.

The jobs czar is right that many firms have relied too much on a now vanishing pool of cheap foreign workers.



But Labour’s leaders must also face the fact that their own policies have led to a million young people being thrown on the scrapheap.

They fail to understand that if you make it more expensive to employ people, firms will simply sit tight and freeze recruitment.

Or even worse, they will rapidly go bust.

The Government has overseen a series of cock-ups which will only make the recruitment for construction work even harder.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The apprentice scheme has been abused, employers have been clobbered and the minimum wage pitched too high.



Can they fix that? Yes they can!

News.title: Child left seriously injured and rushed to hospital after being struck by car in city centre
News.content:
HORROR CRASH Child left seriously injured and rushed to hospital after being struck by car in city centre

A CHILD has been rushed to hospital after being struck by a car in a city centre.

Emergency services were called to Huddersfield Road in Manchester on Saturday following reports of a vehicle collision involving a child.





The victim has been taken to hospital for treatment of their serious injuries.

Greater Manchester Police were alerted to the incident at around 12.35pm on May 23.

At the scene of the horror crash in Oldham, a large police cordon was put in place.

The driver of the car remained at the scene to assist officers.



The force has said that it has not made any arrests yet and is continuing with its investigation into the matter.

The cordon stretching from Asda on Hudderfield Road to Cypress Road has since been lifted.

News.title: Trump vows Strait of Hormuz will reopen as Iran peace deal is being finalised in major breakthrough
News.content:
DONALD Trump has announced that a deal between the US and Iran has been “largely negotiated.”

Details will be announced “shortly” – but the US President confirmed that the Strait of Hormuz will be reopened – after the Islamic Republic and the mediator, Pakistan, submitted a new proposal to end the war in the 11th hour.





In a bombshell post on TruthSocial, he said: “An Agreement has been largely negotiated, subject to finalisation between the United States of America, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and the various other Countries, as listed.

“Final aspects and details of the Deal are currently being discussed, and will be announced shortly.

“In addition to many other elements of the Agreement, the Strait of Hormuz will be opened.”

Leaders of Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Turkey, Egypt, Jordan and Bahrain, as well as ministers of Pakistan, have been pushing to hammer out a final deal.

The post comes after what the US president describes as a “very good call” with leaders from Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Pakistan, Turkey, Jordan and Bahrain.

Trump had a separate call with Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that he said also went “very well”.

He hailed the deal as a “Memorandum of Understanding pertaining to PEACE.”

Major points of contention remain murky – for one, whether Iran will still manage the shipping lane.



Trump also did not mention whether the warring nations had reached an agreement on Iran’s nuclear weapons or the highly enriched uranium.

An official, speaking anonymously, said that Iran and the US had finally made “significant progress” towards a deal but warned that “last-minute disputes” could blow up the efforts.

He said the potential deal would include an official declaration of the war’s end, with two-month negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme.



Meanwhile, Iran had signalled “narrowing differences” in negotiations with the US after Pakistan’s army chief held more talks in Tehran.

Iran’s Fars news ‌agency reported that the theocratic regime would remain under its own management according ⁠to ​the ⁠latest exchanged ⁠text of the deal.

It also dismissed Trump’s announcement of reopening the strait as part ‌of ​a “largely ‌negotiated” deal ⁠as “incomplete ⁠and inconsistent ‌with ​reality.”

“Based on the latest exchanged text, if a possible agreement is reached, the Strait of Hormuz will still be under Iran’s management,” the report from Fars said.

“Although Iran has agreed to allow the number of passing ships to return to the level before the war, this does not at all mean ‘free passage’ to the pre-war situation.



“The management of the strait, determining the route, time, manner of passage, and issuing permits, will remain exclusively under the control and discretion of the Islamic Republic of Iran.”

This is not the first time in recent weeks that a deal has been described as close.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told journalists in India that “there’s been some progress made” and “there may be news later today.”

News.title: White House lockdown LIVE: Suspect dies hours after gunfire breaks out near mansion
News.content:
Gunshots heard near the White House on Saturday May 23 forced Secret Service agents to rush reporters into shelter as authorities investigated the unfolding incident

A man has died after the White House was plunged into lockdown following reports of 20 to 30 gunshots heard in the area Saturday night. President Donald Trump was said to be inside the complex at the time.

Reports on social media showed Secret Service and snipers on the roof and grounds of the presidential residence on Saturday at around 6 p.m.

Shortly after reports emerged on social media about the active shooter at the White House, FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed that law enforcement was on scene investigating the situation. "FBI is on the scene and supporting Secret Service responding to shots fired near White House grounds - we will update the public as we’re able," Patel wrote on X.

Likewise, the Secret Service posted on X that it was "aware of reports of shots fired near 17th Street and Pennsylvania Avenue NW"—one block from the White House— and was "working to corroborate the information with personnel on the ground."

The lockdown has now lifted but investigations are ongoing.

Follow our live blog below for the latest updates.

News.title: UK weather live: Heatwave brings hottest day of year – Met Office says more to come
News.content:
Weather forecasting models suggest the UK could see temperatures rise to 35C as a heatwave grips the country - the Met Office has forecast 33C highs for Monday

UK weather live: Heatwave brings hottest day of year – Met Office says more to come

The Met Office has confirmed the hottest day of the year so far today.

The village of Frittenden, in Kent, hit 30.3C on Saturday and the forecasting body said temperatures are still rising. Before now, Friday had seen the year's warmest temperatures when highs of 28.4C were measured in Heathrow, Cambridge and Cranwell in Lincolnshire.

It comes as the UK faces a days-long heatwave with the Met Office forecasting record breaking temperatures for May. Heat health alerts have been issued by the UKHSA across England.

The UKV weather model now suggests the East of England could reach 35C at around 3pm on Tuesday. And it shows 15 counties at 33C or more - Gloucestershire, Warwickshire, Staffordshire, Norfolk, Suffolk, Leicestershire, Northamptonshire, Cambridgeshire, Oxfordshire, Buckinghamshire, Bedfordshire, Hertfordshire, Essex, Surrey, and Berkshire.

News.title: easyJet could slash flight prices in days as CEO makes Strait of Hormuz promise
News.content:
easyJet could slash flight prices in days as CEO makes Strait of Hormuz promise

Donald Trump has stated a deal is close between the US and Iran - and if the Strait of Hormuz reopens it could mean lower airline prices straight away for passengers

View 3 Images An EasyJet Airbus A320 commercial plane (file photo) (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The boss of easyJet has stated that his airline could slash fares again - if the Strait of Hormuz fully reopens.

‌



The popular budget airline carrier previously said it would raise prices this summer due to the Iran war, with jet fuel now in shorter supply in Europe due to the ongoing situation in the Middle East.

‌



CEO Kenton Jarvis told The Mail on Sunday that the extended closure of Hormuz meant there was "a lot of backed up production that will start flowing" from the region when shipments are once again allowed through the key waterway.

‌



He said: "When the Strait of Hormuz reopens there is going to be an awful lot of supplies that will start shipping out of there."

When asked if easyJet would cut ticket costs for passengers if its fuel bill was lowered by a global price crash, the chief executive replied: 'Yes'.

View 3 Images Vessels anchored in the Strait of Hormuz, off the port city of Khasab on Oman's northern Musandam Peninsula (file image) (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



"The purpose of easyJet is to make flying affordable and accessible and easy for as many people as possible," he continued. "We will always have attractive fares. The reality is that benefit would end up being passed back over time.

"If additional oil fields and wells have been opened in Nigeria, in Norway and in the North Sea, no one's going to shut them down two years later. It's going to bolster the supply globally."

It comes as President Donald Trump stated that a peace deal between the US and Iran is very close, with final aspects of the deal now being discussed.

‌



Donald Trump posted on Truth Social saying: "An Agreement has been largely negotiated, subject to finalization between the United States of America, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and the various other Countries, as listed.

View 3 Images Trump says a deal is close (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"Final aspects and details of the Deal are currently being discussed, and will be announced shortly. In addition to many other elements of the Agreement, the Strait of Hormuz will be opened."

Article continues below

Earlier on Saturday, a regional official with direct knowledge of the Pakistan-led mediation efforts said the U.S. and Iran were closing in on a deal to end the war.

The official, speaking on condition of anonymity to discuss closed-door deliberations, cautioned that “last-minute disputes” could blow up the efforts.

News.title: Aldi, Tesco, Asda and Morrisons announce May Bank Holiday opening times
News.content:
Aldi, Tesco, Asda and Morrisons announce May Bank Holiday opening times

Major UK supermarkets including Lidl, Aldi, Tesco, Asda and Morrisons will be operating different hours during the May Bank Holiday weekend – check opening and closing times before you shop

View 3 Images Shoppers in a supermarket [file image] (Image: SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

This weekend, Brits are set to enjoy an extra day away from work thanks to the late May bank holiday falling on Monday.

‌



While some will opt to unwind and take it easy, others will be making use of their time off to tackle chores including replenishing their fridges and cupboards.

‌



Those planning to utilise the additional day off for supermarket trips need to be mindful of amended opening hours as numerous stores will be shutting earlier and opening later than normal on the bank holiday, reports the Liverpool Echo.

‌



Here are the opening times on Monday, May 25 for Aldi, Lidl, Asda, Sainsbury's, Morrisons, Tesco and M&S.

Aldi

View 3 Images (Image: Liverpool Echo)

Britain's biggest discounter will operate from 8am to 8pm on Monday.

‌



Rachel Geary, communications director at Aldi UK, said: "The late May bank holiday is the perfect chance to enjoy great food, make the most of the longer days and spend quality time with friends and family."

Lidl

Branches outside the M25 and in Wales will trade between 8am and 10pm on Monday. London and Scottish outlets will operate as normal.

Customers are advised to verify everything online before heading out.

‌



Asda

View 3 Images Asda has announced its opening times for Bank Holiday (Image: Google)

Asda branches will trade between 8am and 8pm on the bank holiday. Meanwhile its Asda Express sites typically stay open 24 hours or until their standard late-night closing time.

Sainsbury's

Most supermarkets will operate from 8am until 8pm this coming Monday. The convenience outlets will trade as usual between 7am and 11pm.

‌



Morrisons On bank holiday Monday, most large Morrisons supermarkets across England and Wales will operate from 7am until 8pm. However, the chain noted some branches may shut earlier than usual, depending on your area.

Smaller Morrisons Daily convenience shops will maintain their regular hours.

Tesco

The UK's biggest supermarket chain confirmed that bank holiday Monday opening times will differ by location. Customers are encouraged to verify their local branch hours using the store locator here.

‌



Most large stores and large Express branches throughout England and Wales will trade from 8am until 6pm. Most Isle of Man branches will remain open between 7am and 10pm.

For anyone heading to Scotland for the weekend, large Express branches there will operate from 7am until 10pm. Most large stores and large Express branches in Northern Ireland will maintain their standard hours.

Tesco confirmed that standard Express stores will see no changes to their opening times.

Article continues below

M&S

Marks and Spencer food halls will welcome shoppers slightly later than most rivals, with stores opening at 8.30am and shutting at 6pm.

News.title: Nigel Farage makes 'absurd' claim about Russian hackers and £5m gift
News.content:
Nigel Farage makes 'absurd' claim about Russian hackers and £5m gift

Reform UK chief Nigel Farage faces a standards probe after it emerged he had been given £5million by a Thailand-based cryto billionaire - which he dubbed a "reward for campaigning for Brexit"

View 3 Images Nigel Farage says he had no obligation to declare the gift. (Image: Getty Images)

Nigel Farage now claims Russian spies hacked his phone to obtain details of his controversial £5million gift.

‌



Mr Farage is being probed by the Parliamentary Standards Commissioner over whether he broke Commons rules by not declaring a £5million gift from Christopher Harborne. Mr Farage says he had no obligation to declare the gift.

‌



Sources say the Reform UK leader became ‘intensely suspicious’ that he had been compromised by ‘foreign state actors’ after last month’s revelation about the donation made by Thai-based Christopher Harborne.

‌



View 3 Images Nigel Farage did not think he needed to declare a £5million gift from Christopher Harborne. (Image: Getty Images)

Man falls to his death in Manchester city centre as police investigate unexplained death READ MORE :

Elon Musk turns on Nigel Farage as tech billionaire brands him 'liar' over money offer claims READ MORE :

Reform UK has claimed the cash was “a personal, unconditional gift” with no rules broken. Mr Farage said the money was to pay for his own personal security needs, later describing it as a “reward” for Brexit campaigning.

He faces questions over why he did not declare the £5m he received from Mr Harborne. Parliamentary rules mean new MPs have to declare relevant gifts and donations in the 12 months before their election.

‌



The story about the donation first appeared in The Guardian. There is no suggestion the newspaper was complicit in, or aware of, any illegal activity, but Mr Farage added: "This shocking revelation brings into question The Guardian’s judgment and whether Reform can cooperate with them in future."

In an interview with The Sun, Mr Farage voiced his anger that details of the gift had been made public - saying this was a "disgrace". Asked about the money - which he insists pays for his security, Mr Farage said: "This shouldn't be in the public domain."

View 3 Images Parliamentary rules mean new MPs have to declare relevant gifts and donations in the 12 months before their election. (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



According to MailOnline a source at The Guardian contested Mr Farage’s allegations about its journalism, saying: "This is an absurd claim and an attempt to deflect attention from legitimate scrutiny of his financial affairs. Nigel Farage is once again hiding behind a baseless attack on the media rather than facing up to scrutiny from journalists and politicians. He has repeatedly failed to answer serious public interest questions about the £5 million gift he received."

Nigel Farage now claims Russian spies hacked his phone to obtain details of his controversial £5million gift. A party source said: "Only four people in the world knew about the donation, and so Nigel decided to submit his mobile phone for forensic analysis by counter-espionage experts.

"They concluded that hostile state actors, almost certainly linked to Moscow, had used “spear phishing” tactics to compromise his phone, email and bank accounts."

Article continues below

Mr Farage told The Mail on Sunday: "These actions by Russia are deeply concerning and highlight the threat they pose to British security."

It comes as Nigel Farage insists there is no connection between the £5million gift and his £1.4m house he bought soon afterward.

News.title: Man falls to his death in Manchester city centre as police investigate unexplained death
News.content:
Man falls to his death in Manchester city centre as police investigate unexplained death

Greater Manchester Police rushed to the scene on Charles Street but sadly were unable to save a man who fell from a nearby building - his death is being treated as unexplained

View 2 Images Police at the scene on Charles Street (Image: ASP)

A man has sadly died after falling to his death from a city centre building yesterday.

‌



Greater Manchester Police were called to the scene on Charles Street in Manchester, at around 4pm on Saturday May 23. Sadly a man, who has not been formerly identified, was pronounced dead at the scene.

‌



Reports suggest the Maldron Hotel was evacuated shortly before multiple emergency vehicles and forensic officers were pictured at the scene while a blue forensic tent was put up in the street outside of the Maldron hotel. Police are treating the man's death as unexplained and are continuing with their enquiries.

‌



View 2 Images Police erected a tent on the street (Image: ASP)

Armed officers were seen patrolling the nearby streets in the hours after the tragic incident as the force continues with its investigation into the tragic death.

‌



A Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said: “At around 4pm today (Saturday 23 May 2026), we were called to reports that a man had fallen from a building on Charles Street in the city centre.

“Sadly, a deceased man was found at the scene. Enquiries to establish the full circumstances surrounding his death, which is unexplained, are currently ongoing.”

No further information has been given by police.

Article continues below

The Mirror has contacted the Maldron Hotel for comment.

News.title: TV cameras capture moment gunshots heard at White House as reporters take cover
News.content:
TV cameras capture moment gunshots heard at White House as reporters take cover

The White House is reportedly in lockdown after gunshots were heard outside the building, with reporters quickly evacuated to the press room by Secret Service officials as armed officers responded to the incident

News cameras captured the chilling moment gunshots rang out near the White House.

‌



The building was reportedly placed 'in lockdown' as between 20 to 30 gunshots were heard by journalists outside, who were swiftly escorted into the press room by Secret Service agents.

‌



Fox News reported that the shooter had been taken down by the Secret Service. CNN is now reporting two people have been shot in an encounter with the Secret Service at the White House.

The journalist then shared a photograph of an armed officer stationed outside the door, adding: "Outside the press briefing doors right now...USSS officers, gun drawn, told us to run inside. White House now on lockdown."

‌



Images circulating on social media appeared to show snipers positioned on the roof of the building, alongside another armed officer marching across the White House lawn.

News.title: Starmer urges TNT to make Champions League final free-to-air
News.content:
Sir Keir Starmer has called on TNT Sports to make next Saturday's Champions League final between Arsenal and Paris St-Germain free-to-air.

The UK prime minister has written to the broadcaster to "strongly urge you to reconsider" a decision to make the final available to subscribers only.

Every previous final since the Champions League format was introduced to the European Cup in 1992 has been made available to watch free of charge in the UK.

In a letter to TNT executives, Starmer wrote: "I was saddened to see that, for the first time since the competition started 34 years ago, TNT Sports has decided that [the fixture] will not be free to watch for football supporters here in the UK."

Last week, it was revealed that fans would need a subscription to watch all three European club finals, to which TNT holds the rights.

Starmer - who is an Arsenal fan - wrote: "The Champions League is the biggest club football competition in the world and rightly means a lot to fans in this country - the home of football.

"I am a firm believer that the final of this competition should remain free to watch, whether Arsenal have made it or not.

"Obviously, I want as many fellow fans as possible to be able to watch our team in this historic final for the first time in 20 years. However, this is bigger than that.

"This is about supporters of all teams coming together in living rooms and pubs in every corner of the country to watch the most elite players in Europe battle it out.

"Hard-working people should not have to worry about forking out for a subscription to watch a game of this magnitude.

"We should be putting supporters first. That is why I have already encouraged Fifa to do more to make tickets more affordable at this summer's World Cup.

"That is also why I want to strongly urge you to reconsider and make the final next Saturday free to watch for the millions of passionate football fans in this country."

Fans wanting to watch Aston Villa win the Europa League final last week needed a subscription, and the same will apply to those wanting to watch the Conference League final between Crystal Palace and Rayo Vallecano on Wednesday.

In a statement, TNT Sports said: "It has been a privilege to bring Uefa club competitions to sports fans across the UK throughout the season.

"Having three Premier League clubs reach the finals shows the strength of English football and something that we are proud to continue to support.

"We have made all three Uefa finals this year available from just Â£4.99, the price for a month-long subscription to HBO Max that also includes the great entertainment on the service. This represents exceptional value for fans to watch the conclusion of the competitions."

A nine-story building under construction in a city north of the Philippine capital collapsed early Sunday with 22 workers managing to get out while others remain missing, police said.

The building collapsed before dawn during a thunderstorm in Angeles City in Pampanga province, north of Manila. More than 100 police and other government personnel were scrambling to rescue those believed trapped in the rubble, police Brig. Gen. Jess Mendez said.

Mendez, who was at the scene of the building collapse, said there were no immediate reports of deaths but added that some of the 22 workers who managed to scramble out of the building were injured.

He could not immediately say how many workers were trapped in the collapsed building. But Jay Pelayo, who heads Angeles City’s information office, said at least 30 workers may still be trapped in the rubble, citing a construction foreman who managed to dash out of the building as it tumbled down.

Angeles City used to host one of the largest U.S. Air Force bases outside of the American mainland until it closed in the early 1990s, helping develop Angeles and outlying cities and towns into entertainment and commercial hubs in the main northern Philippine region of Luzon.

The former U.S. Air Force base, now called the Clark Freeport Zone, in Angeles city is about 80 kilometers (50 miles) north of Metro Manila.

Russia attacked Kyiv with missiles and drones overnight Sunday in an intense assault that shook buildings across the city center, including near government offices, residential buildings and schools.

At least 10 people were injured, local authorities said, citing preliminary figures. Air raid sirens blared through the night as smoke billowed across the city from strikes. Associated Press reporters heard powerful explosions near the city center and close to government buildings.

The attack was ongoing by sunrise Sunday, with more missiles and drones expected to reach Kyiv.

Damage was recorded across at least nine districts of the capital including residential buildings, Kyiv military administration head Tymur Tkachenko said in a Telegram post.

In Kyiv’s Shevchenko district, a school building was damaged by an attack while people sheltered inside, Mayor Vitalii Klitschko said. Local authorities reported supermarkets and warehouses across the city also were damaged.

Multiple communities recorded damage throughout the Kyiv region, according to Mykola Kalashnyk, the regional governor.

Earlier, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Russia was planning to use the hypersonic Oreshnik ballistic missile, citing intelligence from the U.S. and Western partners. Ukraine's Air Force later warned of a possible launch of the Oreshnik.

It was not immediately clear if the missile had been used in the overnight attack.

Russia first used the multiple-warhead Oreshnik on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro in November 2024. It was used a second time in January in the western Lviv region.

President Vladimir Putin said the Oreshnik, which means “hazelnut tree” in Russian, streaks at 10 times the speed of sound, or Mach 10, and is capable of destroying underground bunkers “three, four or more floors down.”

The weapon travels “like a meteorite” and is immune to any missile defense system, Putin said, adding that several such missiles, even fitted with conventional warheads, could be as devastating as a nuclear strike.

George Russell landed a double blow on team-mate Kimi Antonelli in Montreal as the gloves came off in the F1 title fight.

The 28-year-old beat his young team-mate to pole position by 0.068 seconds at the Canadian Gand Prix – the same margin as in sprint qualifying on Friday – after being accused of pushing Antonelli off the track in the earlier sprint race.

The title scrap, which had been calm and civilised across the first four races, erupted during the sprint when Antonelli had to take to the grass after banging wheels when trying to overtake Russell at turn one.

Oleksandr Usyk beat Rico Verhoeven in controversial fashion on Saturday, avoiding one of the greatest upsets in boxing history.

Verhoeven, an icon of the kickboxing world, was boxing professionally for just the second time as he challenged Usyk for the WBC heavyweight title – at the pyramids of Giza, no less.

And Verhoeven was arguably on track for a remarkable result, seemingly ahead on points as the 11th round – the penultimate frame – arrived. But it was at that moment that Usyk began to dial up the pressure on Verhoeven, who then walked onto an uppercut in the corner, which dropped him to his knees.

open image in gallery Oleksandr Usyk hurt Rico Verhoeven with an uppercut in the corner, just before the stoppage ( Getty )

Verhoeven beat the referee’s count and was given extra time to recover as his mouthguard was put back in, but when Usyk swarmed the Dutchman with more offence on the ropes, the official waved off the bout as the bell sounded.

Many will have felt that the referee should have let the round finish, while others will argue that Verhoeven was already given extra time to recover from the knockdown.

In any case, the result saw Usyk, 39, maintain his unbeaten record, retain the WBC belt, and avoid a historic upset in Egypt.

Up to that point, the Ukrainian had not looked his usual inventive, spritely self. However, that could have been down to the fine work of Verhoeven, 37, who did well to fight on the front foot for much of the bout, seemingly win the clinch battles, and land clean to the head and body.

Usyk had grown into the fight somewhat after appearing to lose the first few rounds, but it still seemed like he would need a stoppage in the final two rounds to avoid an embarrassing loss.

And Usyk secured that stoppage at 2:59 of round 11, per the official result, with Verhoeven gracious in defeat despite the controversial nature of the ending.

“Yeah, of course, I thought it was an early stoppage, but in the end it’s not up to me,” Verhoeven said in the ring. “But still, I thought it was a little bit early.

“I thought the referee knows that we’re nearly at the end of the round, so let me go out on my shield or let the bell go. But it’s not up to me, and I was already super thankful for the opportunity.”

open image in gallery Rico Verhoeven protesting the referee’s stoppage against Oleksandr Usyk ( Reuters )

Usyk said: “Thank you so much, for me it’s very important, but for me I know right now in Ukraine – my people, my country – are being bombed. My family, my daughter, too, is in a bomb shelter and sent me a message. She said, ‘I know you’ll win.’ I prayed.

“Rico, you’re an amazing fighter, thank you so much. Coach [Peter Fury, uncle of Tyson, who trains Verhoeven], smart. My team, I love you, you are the best. Katarina, my wife, I love you. You’re my life, you’re my heart.”

The Ring magazine’s Rick Reno then brought Agit Kabayel into the ring, with the German expected to be next for Usyk; Kabayel is the unified champion’s mandatory challenger with the WBC, who granted Usyk a voluntary defence against Verhoeven.

However, Saudi matchmaker Turki Alalshikh told Reno that it was “not the time” to push a fight with Kabayel, suggesting that Verhoeven deserved a rematch with Usyk.

Antonelli was told to calm down by race engineer Peter “Bono” Bonnington after his outburst over the radio after the first incident. But when he carried on complaining, he earned a rebuke from his team principal Toto Wolff, who told him to “concentrate on the driving”.

Then, at the end of the race, after Antonelli went off track a third time trying to pass Norris and was looking to vent his spleen again on the cool-down lap, Wolff shut him down a second time. “Kimi, now is not the time to talk about this. We will talk about this later, not on the radio.”

The two Mercedes men had a brief handshake after getting out of their cars, but it promised to be an awkward debrief.

Sky Sports F1 pundit Martin Brundle said it was no surprise to see the two come to blows given they are fighting for the title. Russell is under pressure this weekend because Antonelli has won the last three races to take the championship lead.

“It was always going to happen. Inevitable. Kimi lost his head a little bit but he’ll learn from this,” was Brundle’s verdict.

The fighting at the front was the highlight of an entertaining sprint race in general. Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton looked as if he would take fourth spot for most of the race, only to clip the “Wall of Champions” late in the race. Hamilton was then passed by McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, losing position, which allowed Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc to pass him as well.

News.title: How to have a happy dog and other tips from vets, breeders and trainers
News.content:
Perhaps your dog is easily agitated and you’ve never been able to understand why. According to Dr Wedderburn, the answer might be – and don’t laugh – childhood trauma. “Many, many dogs these days are reactive and get anxious in new situations,” he explains. “They get aggressive and fearful, which is often because they’re badly socialised when they’re young.”

“Puppies have a socialisation window in their brain up until four months of age,” Dr Wedderburn says. “Whenever they come across a new experience, their brain will accept it as being part of the normal world. If they don’t meet experiences until they’re older than that, until they’re maybe five or six months of age, then their brain is fearful and anxious instead and they retain that fear and anxiety for the rest of their lives.”

Trainer Cox has plenty of experience dealing with anxious dogs: “The most important thing is to recognise that the dog is overstimulated and remove them from that environment. Some dogs like gentle stroking, others like a quiet, calm voice or soft food or something else to chew. Maybe a snuffle mat that they can do a little bit of sniffy work – that tends to take their arousal levels down.”

News.title: Leinster humiliated as ruthless Bordeaux retain Champions Cup crown
News.content:
This time there was no Champions Cup final heartbreak for Leinster, just humiliation. In their previous four defeats at the final reckoning, the Irish province could look agonisingly to key moments when the pursuit of a fifth star fell just short.

But this was different. This time there could be no gnashing of teeth, no looking back ruefully at squandered opportunities. This time they came up alarmingly short against a Bordeaux-Bègles side who have, in the eight years since Leinster won the last of their Champions Cup crowns, established themselves as the new European superpower.

The manner in which they retained their title was, quite simply stunning, with all the damage done in a first half that yielded five converted tries, finished by their outstanding captain, Maxime Lucu, Pablo Uberti, Louis Bielle-Biarrey (2) and Yoram Moefana.

They have not lost a Champions Cup game since being beaten by Harlequins in the quarter-finals during the 2023-24 season. The arrival of Tom Willis from Saracens will only strengthen their hand.

News.title: Uganda confirms three more Ebola cases
News.content:
Uganda has confirmed three more Ebola cases as the burgeoning outbreak from neighbouring Congo continues to spread.

Health officials said the new cases brought the total detected in Uganda to five.

Ituri province of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) remains the epicentre of the outbreak but the World Health Organization warned there was a high risk of the infection spreading to other east African countries.

A week after the outbreak was first confirmed, DRC authorities reported that the flare-up was already the third largest on record, with 750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths.

Relief efforts are being hampered by insecurity in Ituri and the fact the outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, rather than the Zaire strain, which caused 15 of the DRC’s previous 17 outbreaks. There are no approved vaccines for the variant, which can kill up to half of those it infects.

News.title: How to get a good night’s sleep when it’s hot and light outside
News.content:
There are plenty of reasons to celebrate a heatwave, but a good night’s sleep is probably not one of them.

You toss and turn, flipping the pillow over and over to try to find the cool side, coated in a sticky sheen of sweat. And the extra daylight is a mixed blessing, making it harder to drop off and trickier to stay asleep once we do.

Light evenings tend to reset our body clock that’s located in our brain. Unfortunately, this is exactly the type we need to feel rested in the morning.

“Our sleep cycle is governed by our sense of light and dark, or circadian rhythm,” explains Dr Guy Meadows, the co-founder and clinical director of the Sleep School app.

The longer we see light, the longer our in internal clock tells our body it is daytime and needs to stay alert. When it gets dark, the body clock signals that it’s time to sleep by releasing melatonin. In summer months we secrete less melatonin, which one reason we wake up earlier and find it harder to drop off.

Temperature is another incredibly important facet of falling asleep, explains Dr Meadows. “Our core body temperature plays an important role in the regulation of sleep. At the start of the night, a 1C drop in temperature is needed to help you fall asleep,” he says. “It’s this decrease, coupled with the arrival of darkness, that informs the internal body clock that the night has begun. This triggers the release of the sleeping hormone melatonin, helping you fall asleep.”

Here, Dr Meadows shares his top tips to sleep in the light and heat:

1. Reduce your exposure to light before preparing for bed

Reducing light use before you head to bed is important, Dr Meadows says. So resist the urge to bask in the evening light.

Draw your blinds to dim the light a good couple of hours before you’re ready to turn in, so that your body begins to step up melatonin production. And don’t forget to switch off electronic devices.

You might also want to invest in blackout blinds – John Lewis do a good range – or at least a sleep mask. Look for masks with adjustable straps that will stay in place and deliver a comfortable, full-blackout.

2. Keep your head cool by keeping a cool head

Dr Meadows adds: “Getting frustrated and restless because you’re too warm only makes your body generate more heat, keeping you awake for longer. Keep cool by lying still and accepting the heat.

“Try focusing your attention on the discomfort and describe what you feel objectively and without judgement, such as ‘I feel heat and sweat on my face, neck and back’. Learning to change your relationship with the heat helps defuse its power and lead to better sleep.”

3. Prepare for cooler sleeping during the daytime

It might sound counter-intuitive, but keeping your curtains closed can stop your bedroom getting warm in the first place, making it easier to fall asleep at night. Another thing to do is to avoid a late dinner.

“Eating food close to bedtime elevates your body temperature, making it harder to sleep,” says Dr Meadows. “For the best night’s sleep, leave at least two hours between eating and sleeping – and limit alcohol consumption.”

4. Wear cotton pyjamas or sleep naked

“If you’re wearing natural fibres like cotton, then you’ll feel cooler in the night than if you were naked, because the cotton will wick away sweat from your skin,” says Dr Alanna Hare, an NHS and private sleep consultant at the Royal Brompton Hospital.

“However, anything man-made or synthetic will keep heat next to your skin. And the same goes for bedding. So if I had the choice between cotton and nakedness, I’d choose cotton. But if you’re choosing between man-made fibres and nakedness, go naked.”

5. Create a breeze

“Sleep with the window open or keep a fan on during the night to add an extra breeze in your bedroom,” Dr Meadows advises.

If you want to keep things extra cool, place a frozen bottle of water between yourself and the fan to cool the air as it comes towards you. (Modern air coolers can chill the room by a few degrees using this principle, although they’re not as effective as refrigerating air conditioners.)

6. Make a ‘cold water bottle’

“Simply fill a hot water bottle with cold water and keep it in the fridge or freezer for a few hours before bed – if you’re an extra hot sleeper, you can leave it in a little longer,” suggests Chris Tattersall, a sleep expert at bedding manufacturer Woolroom.

“Then snuggle up with your ice pack under the covers or leave it to cool down the bed before jumping in – it’s one of the best ways to keep cool at night.”

7. Ditch the memory foam

“The synthetic materials used in a memory foam mattress mean that it’s not breathable and doesn’t absorb moisture, leaving your body to overheat and sweat while in bed,” says Tattersall.

“You know that sinking feeling you get when you sleep on a memory foam mattress? For that to happen, it needs body heat to warm it up, which is then reflected back onto you as you sleep.

“Overlaying your memory foam mattress with a wool mattress protector will help regulate around 75 per cent of that heat, helping you stay cooler on those hot summer evenings.”

Sports.title: From model once linked to Michael B Jordan to glam nurse – meet England World Cup wags set to bring glamour to the game
Sports.content:
OUR Three Lions will not be the only England team attracting plenty of attention at the World Cup next month.

The latest squad of Wags will command their own share of the limelight in North America.





There are players in boss Thomas Tuchel’s party who have been to a World Cup before but others, and their wives or girlfriends, will be experiencing the excitement for the first time.

It is 20 years since the World Cup in Germany when England’s Wags took centre stage with their wild partying.

Here are some to look out for this year . . .

Mia McClenaghan & Reece James



CHELSEA defender Reece has dated glamorous law graduate, model and influencer Mia for six years.

A year after going public, Reece, 26, and Mia, 25, posed in matching baby blue track-suits in what was thought to be their new home.

She graduated from London’s Royal Holloway University in 2021 and reportedly worked at HMP Coldingley in Surrey, giving legal advice to inmates.



She has also shared glam posts on Instagram, where she has around 27,000 followers.

Naima Corbin & Eberechi Eze

ARSENAL midfielder Eze is now a Premier League champion – but kept grounded by wife Naima who is a nurse.

He has said: “I come home thinking about X, Y and Z then get a reality check with my wife. She works in an intensive care unit. I love that part of my life so much. It humbles you.”

The couple, both 27, met at school and were legally married in 2022 before celebrating twice more last year – with a Nigerian ceremony in a nod to his African parentage, then a reception in a Thames-side gothic mansion.



The player proposed to Naima in the five-star Shangri-La hotel at London landmark The Shard.

It was mid-Covid and they wore masks.

Naima swerves social media, to keep her personal life private.

Layla Roye & Kobbie Mainoo



STUDENT and model Layla is the rumoured love interest of Manchester United midfielder Kobbie.

The 22-year-old from Manchester is working towards a fashion, business and promotion degree at the University of Salford.

Layla, who is signed to a modelling agency, says: “I am passionate about the world of luxury fashion and its ability to blend creativity, culture and commerce.”

She and Kobbie, 21, have not confirmed their relationship but did share tell-tale social media posts on holiday in Dubai earlier this year.

They did not pose together but fans spotted matching backgrounds in their pictures.



Ellie & Ollie Watkins

ASTON VILLA frontman Ollie’s wife Ellie looks quite striking herself, in a bikini.

Ollie, 30, met interior designer Ellie, 29, on the beach in Marbella while she was on a post-university girls’ holiday in 2018, and their love match has grown from there.

He proposed to her in Italy in 2024, beside Lake Como, and the couple tied the knot in London in May last year before hosting a three-day celebration in the South of France.



They now have two children together.

Ollie, who is in the World Cup squad, won the Europa League with Villa this week, with Ellie sharing celebratory snaps from the pitch with her 80,000 Instagram followers.

Despite the couple’s lavish lifestyle, Ellie still likes to make a bob or two flogging her old clothes on shopping app Depop.

Ashlyn Castro & Jude Bellingham



REAL Madrid midfielder Jude’s girlfriend Ashlyn is a Californian model and influencer.

Ashlyn, 28, who has 648,000 followers on Instagram, once dated US basketball star Terance Mann, and was linked to Hollywood hottie Michael B Jordan, who at this year’s Oscars won Best Actor gong for horror movie Sinners.

Ashlyn and Jude, 22, met online in late 2024 then went public in 2025.

They have spent a lot of time together while he recovered from a shoulder op last summer, and then a more recent hamstring injury.

She has called him “the most thoughtful, kind-hearted, hard-working, incredible human I’ve ever met”.



Last year, she took to social media to hit back at trolls and clear up rumours about her dating, saying: “I’ve had three boyfriends over the last eight years.”

Olivia and John Stones

JOHN will have more than one reason to celebrate if England make the World Cup Final – it will be the day after his first wedding anniversary.

The 31-year-old centre back, who will leave Man City this summer, married property developer Olivia, 37, at an intimate ceremony in Ibiza on July 18 last year, which was followed by a poolside party the next day.



The footie final will be on July 19.

They began dating in 2019 and had a son in 2023.

They both have children from previous relationships.

Millie & Dean Henderson

CRYSTAL PALACE goalie Dean made a great catch – wife Millie has been his rock throughout his football career and two bereavements.



Dean, 29, married Millie in 2022 during a lavish bash in Italy, at Rome’s Villa Miani hotel, where singer Lewis Capaldi performed for guests.

She then consoled him after the death of his dad Dougie in 2024, and when pal George Baldock died at 31 the same year.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The pair played together while Dean was on loan at Sheffield Utd.

Dean and Millie have a two-year-old son, and their daughter was born in December.

Sports.title: Liverpool warned not to make ‘very stupid’ Arne Slot sack decision with season woes blamed on ‘coach killer’ Mo Salah
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL would be “very stupid” if they sacked Arne Slot because their issues this season are all down to poor recruitment and “coach killer” Mo Salah.

Slot’s old mentor Jan Everse, who was capped twice for Holland’s 1970s Total Football team, has given a damning assessment of the Reds.





Though it has been a difficult season, Liverpool are on the cusp of Champions League qualification.

Everse, who managed Slot when he was 17 at FC Zwolle, said: “The worst thing that can happen to Arne is that they fire him. But they would be very stupid.

“Jurgen Klopp was at Liverpool for nine years with Liverpool.

“Slot came in and he became champion. Everybody was happy.



“And now one player is not satisfied because he’s played bad.

“You will now see them competing for the title again.”

Slot’s relationship with Salah, 33, hit rock bottom when the Egyptian gave an explosive interview claiming Liverpool had “thrown me under the bus”.

Last weekend, he fired a parting shot at Slot on social media by urging the team to play Klopp’s “heavy-metal football”.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Everse, 72, says he noticed a while back that Salah was not producing the goods and during the first fallout last December he got in touch with his protege.

Everse said: “I said stay strong, Salah’s playing bad. He is not passing defenders any more.

“He was a great player.

“He decided many games which were important for Liverpool. But Salah is 100 per cent a coach killer.”



Everse also does not think the seven new signings made by the hierarchy have worked out.

He added: “The problem was they bought so many players and it always takes time.”

Sports.title: ‘Don’t need a break’ – Michael Carrick axes summer holidays just days after landing permanent Man Utd job
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK says he will not need a break before getting stuck into his first summer as boss of Manchester United.

The Red Devils finally confirmed Carrick’s permanent appointment on a two-year deal on Friday after 11 wins in 16 games since being named interim gaffer on January 13.





Carrick guided United to Champions League qualification and third place with matches to spare and he is now braced for his first summer transfer window in charge of the club.

The 44-year-old had his holiday in Barbados during the Christmas and New Year period interrupted when Old Trafford chiefs contacted him about potentially taking over.

Carrick will not be jetting off after United’s final game of the season at Brighton today as his daughter, Louise, and son, Jacey, are doing their exams.

And the Red Devils legend said he does not require a holiday to recharge the batteries ahead of his biggest season in management.

Carrick said: “It’s the kids’ exams that are getting in the way at the moment, A-levels and GCSEs. That’s stopping me from booking anything.

“To be honest, I don’t need a break. I feel good. I think you get in the rhythm of working, really, in different ways.”

Speaking to journalists, he added: “I’m sure you have different hours to what I do.

“Some of you work more than others, I’m sure you do. You get used to it, you get into the flow of it.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“I’ve loved it, I’ve loved every minute of it, so I certainly don’t feel that I need a break.”

United’s non-international players are scheduled to return for pre-season training the week beginning July 5.

The club’s first friendly is against Hollywood-owned Wrexham in the Finnish capital Helsinki on July 18.

They have also scheduled friendlies with Norway’s Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atletico Madrid in Stockholm, Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg and Leeds in Dublin.

Carrick’s men are set to return to Ireland for a pre-season training camp, having enjoyed a three-night stay at Carton House last month.



A sixth friendly against AC Milan in the Polish city of Wroclaw could also be announced before the Premier League season starts on August 22.

United are planning for at least four key signings, with two midfielders, a forward and a left-back wanted.

The club are prepared to move for a third midfielder if Manuel Ugarte is sold and could recruit a back-up goalkeeper.



United’s preference is for recruits aged between 22 and 26 after the impacts of summer signings Brazilian striker Matheus Cunha, 26, Cameroon attacker Bryan Mbeumo, 26, Slovenian forward Benjamin Sesko, 22, and Belgian goalkeeper Senne Lammens, 23.

But Carrick has also seen younger players Kobbie Mainoo, 21, Leny Yoro, 20, and Ayden Heaven, 19, mature on his watch.

Carrick said: “I’ve seen that, for sure. I’ve seen development, a lot of development in different ways. Some of it you see on the pitch, it’s obvious it’s there performance-wise.

“There’s a technical part of it and the players are improving in that regard.



“But sometimes it’s feeling comfortable in the best way of being here, and knowing what it feels like to play here, having an element of success, having an element of a few challenges.

“You come through it and you understand what it takes to get through it. I think that as much as anything.

“And then you can grow, your character and personality comes out even more, I’ve seen that for some of the younger players.

“And actually not just the younger players, you can see that everyone is growing a little bit more when you’re getting good results with good performances.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“So I think leadership’s different from everyone. I think there are some leader examples, some show it a little bit more vocally.

“But you can definitely see each and every player grow when you’re moving in the right direction, for sure.”

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi blames Spurs’ relegation woes on stars CARING too much – despite Cristian Romero fleeing to Argentina
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM boss Roberto De Zerbi believes they are in the relegation mire because his flops care TOO MUCH.

Questions over the squad’s commitment hang over Spurs’ drop battlers after a week in which skipper Cristian Romero deserted them.





A point would guarantee survival — sending West Ham down to the Championship — regardless of whether Nuno Espirito Santo’s side beat Leeds or not.

Yet crocked captain Romero, 28, has snubbed his own team in favour of watching boyhood side Belgrano’s title play-off with River Plate back in Argentina — making himself Public Enemy No 1 among Tottenham fans.

It means, once again, the armband will be with Dutch centre-back Micky van de Ven, 25, who had to defend himself and his team-mates in March against accusations over their commitment to the cause.

For De Zerbi, the North London side go into Sunday’s clash against Everton without a Prem home win in five months because the situation has got under their skin.

Asked about suggestions his players did not care enough, the Italian hit back: “No, absolutely false. No, no, no, it’s not true. It’s totally different, maybe they suffered too much. Their reaction has not been right but not for that reason.

“They are sensitive guys and they have suffered the situation. Maybe they didn’t know how they can get out of this situation?

“But there is just one solution to get out — to be strong, stronger than the atmosphere of the situation, or the injuries, or the negative things. They suffer.”

Whether fans will buy that their players are going through the mill as much as they are is doubtful, having been let down by them time and again across this dreadful campaign.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But the fact is you would much rather be in Tottenham’s position right now than West Ham’s.

And for that, supporters are crossing their fingers, toes and everything in between that their team can buck the trend of caving when the heat is on and see it out.

Spurs could have wrapped up survival already had they not lost 2-1 to Chelsea on Tuesday.

But De Zerbi, who took over with just seven games to go and the club in the relegation zone by the time he kicked off his first match, admits he would have taken this final-day scenario were it offered to him.



The Italian said: “Yes, I didn’t come here in mid-table. The secret is to manage the pressure. Just that. To manage the pressure you have to be clear and honest with yourself.

“The level of difficulty of the game is high. We are fighting for something very important for everyone.

“It is football — but we have enough quality and we are playing in our stadium.”

Final day relegation scenarios THERE are ten possible scenarios that could decide who is relegated between Tottenham and West Ham on Sunday.. Scenario 1: Spurs win, West Ham win – West Ham relegated Scenario 2: Spurs win, West Ham draw – West Ham relegated Scenario 3: Spurs win, West Ham lose – West Ham relegated Scenario 4: Spurs draw, West Ham win – West Ham relegated Scenario 5: Spurs draw, West Ham draw – West Ham relegated Scenario 6: Spurs draw, West Ham lose – West Ham relegated Scenario 7: Spurs draw, West Ham win by 13 goals – Spurs relegated Scenario 8: Spurs lose, West Ham win – Spurs relegated Scenario 9: Spurs lose, West Ham draw – West Ham relegated Scenario 10: Spurs lose, West Ham lose – West Ham relegated

De Zerbi is expecting Daniel Farke’s Leeds side to test the Hammers, as they did Spurs when they drew 1-1 almost a fortnight ago.



RDZ added: “Everton will be a tough game for us, but it will be a tough game for West Ham, too.

“West Ham play Leeds and I’m sure Leeds will play like they did in the Tottenham stadium (when they drew 1-1).”

De Zerbi has experienced relegation as a manager before, dropping out of Serie A with Benevento in 2018.

He claimed there can be no comparisons between the two situations because Spurs are a bigger club.

But he did learn an awful lot from the demotion from Serie A in how to deal with a squad that is fighting for their lives.



He explained: “It was a very important experience for me because if you play to compete, to win, you have enthusiasm, you have a good feeling in the week, in the meetings.

“When you are fighting against relegation and have all the players in front of you, the eyes of the players are not like the players when you are winning a league, or you are competing to achieve European qualification.

“It’s totally different. You have to be positive, you have to take the players with you and convince the players.



“You have to find the balance to push and to be strong with them but also to give hugs to transfer confidence.”

That is exactly what De Zerbi has tried to do since taking over Spurs’ sinking ship.

He has relentlessly talked up the players’ abilities, downplaying their shortcomings and not dwelling on any perceived injustices.

He has even played old YouTube highlights reels of their best moments to remind them of what they can do.

The career highlight to date for many will be last season’s memorable and glorious Europa League triumph in Bilbao over Manchester United — the anniversary for which was on Thursday.



But De Zerbi says the pressure of that final will feel like nothing compared to what his players have to face this afternoon.

He added: “It’s easier to play the final of Europa League than to play Tottenham versus Everton, 100 per cent.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“As a pressure it’s totally different. But if we win this game there is another pride, another emotion, another feeling.”

Spurs fans will be desperately hoping that feeling is one of relief come 6pm on Sunday night – then they can let out the raw emotion when their Premier League pride remains intact.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso told he’s inheriting ‘best academy in world’ as Calum McFarlane signs off from second Chelsea manager stint
Sports.content:
XABI ALONSO will inherit a host of teenage talent when he takes over at Chelsea, says interim boss Calum McFarlane.

Ex-Real Madrid head coach Alonso will be under pressure to add ready-made stars over the summer to a squad lacking experience.





But Blues regular Under-21s gaffer McFarlane, 40, assured the Spaniard the Cobham conveyor belt will still provide him with blue-chip youth options.

McFarlane, who signs off from first-team duty at Sunderland, said: “It’s the best ­academy in the world.

“I have specific knowledge, having worked with a lot of the players in older age groups.

“There are lots of players who can make the jump.”



Ryan Kavuma-McQueen, 17, and Jesse Derry, 18, have made first-team debuts this season.

And Shim Mheuka, 18, has made four sub senior appearances for the West London club.

McFarlane added: “It’s part of the DNA. That is never going to stop.”

Alonso, 44, will have the job of leading Chelsea back into Champions League football next season.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The club can only finish as high as 7th in the Premier League this term if they beat the Black Cats and Brighton fail to beat Manchester United.

This means, in the best case, the club would be competing in the Conference League – a tournament they won in 2025.

The U18s have achieved success this season, having beaten United to the age-group’s Premier League title.

That team included the likes of Derry and Kavuma-McQueen as well as other prospects such as Mathis Eboue, Chizaram Ezenwata and Reggie Watson.



If the Blues continue to struggle on the pitch, then any of them could see opportunities come their way.

McFarlane is mainly focused on ending his spell in charge of the first-team with a positive result at the Stadium of Light.

Though he has admitted he is not thinking about the chance of securing European football with a win.

He added: “There’s no point thinking about that really.

“We knew from the beginning of the season that we’d have Sunderland on the last day of the season.



“So we need to face what’s in front of us. We’re more than capable of going there and winning that game.

“But we know we have to be at our best to get three points because they’re a very good side.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It would be a disappointment if we don’t win on Sunday. That’s all our focus is on is beating Sunderland.



“We can’t control the other results. We’ll be fully focused on getting three points against Sunderland.”

Sports.title: Gareth Southgate's net worth, enormous England salary, wife he met in Tesco car park
Sports.content:
Gareth Southgate's net worth, enormous England salary, wife he met in Tesco car park

Gareth Southgate's England reign will be the focus of a new BBC drama

View 3 Images Gareth Southgate will be played by Joseph Fiennes in a four-part BBC drama (Image: BBC/Left Bank/Getty/Justin Downing/Anthony Pileggi)

England's first major tournament since Gareth Southgate's departure is looming large. Southgate managed the Three Lions for eight years, reaching the finals of both Euro 2020 and Euro 2024.

‌



England also surprisingly reached the last four of the 2018 World Cup under his watch and re-established the team as a major force in the world game following abject performances at the 2014 World Cup and Euro 2016. Southgate has kept a low profile since stepping down in the wake of the defeat to Spain in Berlin two years ago.

‌



However, the successes and challenges of his reign will be relived in a new BBC drama, Dear England, which begins on Sunday. The four-part series is based on James Graham's award-winning play of the same name, which focuses on Southgate and the England team during his tenure.

‌



Ahead of the series, here's the lowdown on Southgate's net worth, huge England salary and how he met his wife…

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

England salary

Southgate was handsomely rewarded for his tenure as England boss, with an annual salary of around £5m. This made him the highest-paid manager at Euro 2024, just ahead of Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann £4.8m.

‌



Despite finishing as runners-up, over £20m in prize money was secured. This sum was partially distributed among the 26-man squad, with Southgate and his staff receiving bonuses from the pot.

Thomas Tuchel is the 'double' of Sir Alf Ramsey in bid for World Cup glory READ MORE :

Net worth

While some brand him boring, others would call him sensible. Either way, it has contributed to financial success away from football management.

After becoming England manager, he established a company, FHS Promotions Limited, to manage his image rights and endorsements while building an impressive property portfolio. That has helped Southgate establish an estimated net worth of around £9m.

‌



View 3 Images Southgate turned England's fortunes around (Image: Clive Rose/Getty Images)

Meeting wife in car park

Given his football earnings, Southgate and his family can afford a luxurious lifestyle. However, there was nothing fancy about his early rendezvous with wife Alison.

According to OK , it was a Tesco car park that set the foundations for their relationship. Prior to that, Southgate would meekly hang out by a local shop to catch a glimpse of his crush, despite the fact she had a boyfriend at the time.

‌



That didn’t deter him, and he eventually plucked up the courage to hand Alison his phone number after sussing out she was on the verge of a break-up. And it was the superstore where they would secretly meet before they officially became an item.

View 3 Images The Southgates have been married for almost 30 years (Image: Getty Images)

Alison Bird became Mrs Southgate in July 1997. Despite her husband having a successful playing career with Crystal Palace, Aston Villa, and Middlesbrough, and then holding the biggest job in English football for eight years, she has never been passionate about the game.

‌



Clive Southgate, Gareth’s father, previously told the Daily Mail: "Actually, I don't think Alison likes football very much.

"Obviously she has to take an interest because it’s Gareth’s job, and she is always very supportive. She will sometimes go to Wembley for an international game but not during the school term because she always puts the children first."
